subject: How could I include an interaction effect in the model, and can I use a continous variable?

messages.author: 9496e89c82a47887
messages.subject: How could I include an interaction effect in the model, and can I use a continous variable?
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use methylKit for RRBS data (~50 samples)

Question 1:
I would like to test a model like so: Y = A + B + A*B (where A is group and B is age)

In the "Accounting for covariates" section of the manual from my understanding in calculateDiffMeth() I can only include B as a covariate, but it is not clear to me how I could include the interaction A*B.


Question 2:
I would also like to test a model where instead of group I would have a continuous variable, i.e., Y = C (where C is a continuous variable)
Is this at all possible?

Thank you.

Best,
Isabel

On Fri, May 15, 2020 at 1:20 PM Isabel <isabel.s...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,

I am trying to use methylKit for RRBS data (~50 samples)

Question 1:
I would like to test a model like so: Y = A + B + A*B (where A is group and B is age)

In the "Accounting for covariates" section of the manual from my understanding in calculateDiffMeth() I can only include B as a covariate, but it is not clear to me how I could include the interaction A*B.
You can not do this at the moment. You need to set up the model yourself and iterate through the lines.

Question 2:
I would also like to test a model where instead of group I would have a continuous variable, i.e., Y = C (where C is a continuous variable)
Is this at all possible?

This may work if you set up numeric values per sample for the treatment. If it doesn't work you have to use the approach I described above.

Best,
altuna
 
Thank you.

Best,
Isabel
